verses.text: This is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.
He said, “Yahweh came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to them. He shone from Mount Paran. He came from the ten thousands of holy ones. At his right hand was a fiery law for them.
Yes, he loves the people. All his saints are in your hand. They sat down at your feet. Each receives your words.
Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together.
“Let Reuben live, and not die; Nor let his men be few.”
This is for Judah. He said, “Hear, Yahweh, the voice of Judah. Bring him in to his people. With his hands he contended for himself. You shall be a help against his adversaries.”
About Levi he said, “Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one, whom you proved at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father, and of his mother, ‘I have not seen him.’ He didn’t acknowledge his brothers, nor did he know his own children; for they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.
They shall teach Jacob your ordinances, and Israel your law. They shall put incense before you, and whole burnt offering on your altar.
Yahweh, bless his skills. Accept the work of his hands. Strike through the hips of those who rise up against him, of those who hate him, that they not rise again.”
About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of Yahweh will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he said, “His land is blessed by Yahweh, for the precious things of the heavens, for the dew, for the deep that couches beneath,
for the precious things of the fruits of the sun, for the precious things that the moon can yield,
for the best things of the ancient mountains, for the precious things of the everlasting hills,

for the precious things of the earth and its fullness, the good will of him who lived in the bush.  Let this come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who was separated from his brothers.

The firstborn of his herd, majesty is his. His horns are the horns of the wild ox. With them he will push all the peoples, to the ends of the earth. They are the ten thousands of Ephraim. They are the thousands of Manasseh.”
About Zebulun he said, “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out; and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call the peoples to the mountain. There they will offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they will draw out the abundance of the seas, the hidden treasures of the sand.”
About Gad he said, “He who enlarges Gad is blessed. He dwells as a lioness, and tears the arm, yes, the crown of the head.

He provided the first part for himself, for the lawgiver’s portion reserved was reserved for him. He came with the heads of the people. He executed the righteousness of Yahweh, His ordinances with Israel.”
About Dan he said, “Dan is a lion’s cub that leaps out of Bashan.”
About Naphtali he said, “Naphtali, satisfied with favor, full of Yahweh’s blessing, Possess the west and the south.”
About Asher he said, “Asher is blessed with children. Let him be acceptable to his brothers. Let him dip his foot in oil.
Your bars will be iron and brass. As your days, so your strength will be.
“There is no one like God, Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens for your help, in his excellency on the skies.
The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, ‘Destroy!’
Israel dwells in safety; the fountain of Jacob alone, In a land of grain and new wine. Yes, his heavens drop down dew.

You are happy, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by Yahweh, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency? Your enemies will submit themselves to you. You will tread on their high places.”

footnotes.content: Here Moses stands at the end of forty years, his task nearly finished, and turns to bless the people he's led. Before death comes, blessing—what a beautiful order. The Lord does the same with us, giving grace to speak His words into the lives we've touched.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sinai, Seir, Paran—the great holy places where God showed Himself—all point to this one truth: the Lord comes to His people with fire, law, and covenant. Ten thousands of holy ones surround Him; we are never outside His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "He loves the people." Not begrudgingly. Not because they earned it. The saints sit at His feet like children eager to hear His word. That's where belonging starts—not in our striving, but in His love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The law is called an inheritance—not a burden to escape, but a gift passed down through generations. Moses gave them something to hold onto when he was gone. That's what a faithful life leaves behind.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In Jeshurun—Israel's poetic name, meaning "upright one"—the Lord was King when all the tribes gathered in unity. I've learned that the Lord loves unity because it lets His kingdom show itself most clearly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reuben, the firstborn who stumbled, receives a blessing of life and increase. The Lord does not erase our failings; He blesses us forward from them. That mercy has followed me all my days.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judah contended for himself with his own hands—strong, wrestling, determined—yet Moses asks that the Lord bring him to his people and be his help. Even strength finds its rest in God's strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thummim and Urim—the priestly lots by which God's will was sought. Levi was proven at Massah and Meribah, the places of Israel's complaint and thirst. From testing came priesthood, from doubt came closeness to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levi separated himself from family ties to keep God's word and covenant—a costly faithfulness. Yet in losing family for His sake, they gain the whole household of faith. I've seen that trade make whole what it seemed to break.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Teaching, burning incense, offering sacrifices—Levi's work is to draw near to God on Israel's behalf. The priests stand between heaven and earth, showing that all blessing flows from the One above.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Bless his skills"—God cares about the work of our hands, the gifts we've been given. And when enemies rise, the Lord breaks them so they cannot stand again. His strength covers us in our labor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin, the beloved, dwells in safety between the Lord's shoulders—carried, protected, resting. That's the promise for any who will lean into His care. He covers us all the day long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joseph's land blessed with heavenly dew and the deep waters beneath—earth and sky poured out. The Lord gives not from scarcity but from abundance, even to those the world has cast out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sun and moon yield their precious gifts to this one land. I've noticed how the Lord seems to bless the work of His faithful people with an overflow—the ordinary seasons become extraordinary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ancient mountains and everlasting hills—the oldest things we know—pour their treasures into Joseph's portion. The Lord's care reaches back to creation itself and flows forward to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The burning bush—God dwelling in fire, separated from the nations, yet His favor came to Joseph alone. To be set apart for God is to be honored beyond measure, even in suffering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim and Manasseh—the firstborn of Joseph—possess the strength of wild oxen, pushing forward to the earth's ends. From exile and loss came multitude and might. The Lord restores with interest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zebulun and Issachar together—one in tents, one going out. Some are called to dwell, some to labor. Both are blessed when each honors their calling and they walk in joy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They call peoples to the mountain to offer sacrifices of righteousness and draw treasures from sea and sand. Their commerce and worship are one—all labor is made holy when offered to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gad—a tribe dwelling east of Jordan—is likened to a lioness, fierce and royal. Even those living on the edge of the promise are not forgotten; their strength has its place in God's kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gad received the lawgiver's portion first and executed the Lord's righteousness with His ordinances. To be chosen first is to serve first. Leadership is measured not by receiving but by doing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan is a lion's cub leaping from Bashan—youth, strength, bold courage. Even the smallest tribe is mighty when it springs from the heart God has given it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali, satisfied with favor, possesses west and south. When the Lord's blessing fills us, we lack nothing and can claim what the Lord has given us without fear or want.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asher is blessed with children and dips his foot in oil—abundance and acceptance among brothers. The Lord gives both fruitfulness and favor in family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Iron and brass bars—strong defenses—yet the true promise is that strength matches the days. We are never given more than we can bear. Each day brings exactly what we need.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is no one like God—Moses turns to the whole people now with certainty. He who rides the heavens for your help, in glory above the skies. All other gods fade to shadow beside Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these words: the eternal God is our dwelling place; underneath are everlasting arms. When we have nowhere else to go, we have Him. He thrusts out our enemies and bids us be free.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel dwells in safety—alone, yes, but not abandoned. The fountain of Jacob, land of grain and wine, dew from heaven. Isolation becomes privilege when the Lord makes it so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You are happy, Israel!" The final word is joy. Saved by the Lord, shielded and made excellent, treading on high places where once you stumbled. This blessing is the benediction not just for a people, but for any soul who knows His saving grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
